title: Customer Compliance Intake Hub — automated questionnaire routing, regional retention controls, and audit bundle exports
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build a self-serve Compliance Intake Hub for customer compliance requests that: 1) ingests standard questionnaire templates (SOC2, ISO, custom RFPs) and routes to the right internal owner, 2) provides a guided DPA helper that auto-populates customer details and generates a draft DPA bundle for legal review, 3) surfaces and allows customer-configurable data residency and retention settings in the Console, and 4) exports an auditable evidence bundle with signed artifacts and retention proofs. Goal: reduce mean time to evidence and DPA turnaround from weeks to days and lower support engineering load for routine requests.
scope: MVP covers intake UI, questionnaire template registry, routing rules, exportable evidence ZIP with logs and config, basic DPA draft generator (templated sections only), and Console toggles for regional residency and retention windows. Integrations: Console API, Support ticketing (Zendesk/GH), KMS audit logs, and S3 export.
non_goals: This project will not replace full legal DPA negotiations, implement organization-wide RBAC for enterprise customers (that is a follow-up), or build an on-prem installer for the Private product. Full automated legal signing is out of scope.
success_metrics: Reduce average evidence request SLA from 12 business days to <= 3 business days
>50% of inbound questionnaire requests handled without manual Support/Eng intervention
DPA draft generation used in >= 30% of new enterprise sales engagements within first quarter post-release
Audit bundle exports verified by at least 3 pilot customers
acceptance_criteria: Customers can submit a questionnaire and receive an assigned owner and SLA within the UI
DPA helper outputs a pre-populated draft with customer fields and a link to start legal review
Console exposes data residency selector (region list) and retention window selector per-customer and persists to config API
Evidence export contains logs, configuration snapshot, retention proof, and signed hashes; export can be downloaded and attached to support ticket
Operational runbook exists: how to escalate, manual overrides, and how to ingest custom questionnaire types
comments: 2025-02-18 — Priya Nair: Initial brief and scope. PM kickoff with Legal and Support. Identified top customer asks: DPA templating, residency by region, and single-click evidence export.

2025-02-25 — Diego Ramos: Discovery complete. Interviewed three mid-market customers and Support queue. Customers want a way to exclude ephemeral logs from evidence exports — added to acceptance criteria.

2025-03-02 — Alex Morgan (Engineering): Proposed architecture: intake service + job queue + export worker. Concern: KV cache for evidence snapshots could be large; recommending streamed export to S3 to avoid memory spikes. Assigned ENG-6120 for infra work.

2025-03-04 — Emily Chen (Design): Shared prototype link. Key decision: combine questionnaire submit + residency selector on the same flow for clarity. Raised accessibility checklist items. DES-1423 created for UI polish.

2025-03-07 — Legal (Marta Alvarez): Reviewed DPA template approach. OK with draft generation as long as each generated DPA is flagged and logged for review; Legal requests retention of change history for DPA drafts.

2025-03-10 — Diego Ramos: Implemented mock export and shared initial PoC with Support. Manual QA passed for 2 of 3 test scenarios; edge case failures for very large log exports documented in ENG-6120.
2025-03-12 — Priya Nair: Prioritization sync: move automated routing rules (region-based owner selection) to phase 1 because it eliminates manual triage. Added to scope and updated estimate.
2025-03-12 — QA (Jordan Li): Test plan drafted. Called out security checklist: ensure export artifacts are encrypted in transit and at rest; validate signed hashes as part of acceptance criteria.
notes: Trade-off: fully automated DPA signing vs legal oversight — MVP uses drafted DPA + legal queue to avoid legal/regulatory mistakes
Decision: Store retention metadata at customer resource level (Console) rather than per-request to simplify export logic
Risk: Evidence export may include PII if customers misconfigure — add confirmation and PII scan step before export (low-latency heuristic)
